head: claude/mi69-automerge-misfire
title: automerge: gate the relay on the branch's OWN request, and stop it un-drafting
body:
Stops `claude-pr-automerge` un-drafting and arming PRs that asked for nothing. **Three were armed this way at 2026-09-02T13:19Z**, and two are still armed right now (see the ⚠️ below — that half is not fixed by this PR and needs someone with write access).

## ⚠️ The dispatched diagnosis was wrong, and the prescribed fix would have fixed nothing

I was sent to remove the legacy shared path `.github/pr-automerge-request` from the `paths:` filter, on the reading — in the dispatch and in `BL-20260902-A-REBASE-ARMS-AUTOMERGE-...` — that a rebase drags that path in. **Measured before changing anything, on all three mis-fires, taking the push diff as GitHub computes it (`parent1..merge`):**

```
$ git diff --name-only 9cf89802^1 9cf89802 -- \
    '.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt' '.github/pr-automerge-request'
.github/pr-automerge-requests/claudebot-answerable.txt
.github/pr-automerge-requests/manager-concurrency-cap.txt
```
Same shape for `5449ef6c` and `31cff960`. **The legacy path is in ZERO of the three.** It had not been modified on `main` since 2026-08-21 (`fd6c2cab`), so it could not match a 2026-09-02 rebase.

What matched is the **per-request glob itself** — the path the dispatch called "already the documented convention". Nine `*.txt` request files landed on `main` on 2026-09-02 alone, so any branch merging `main` drags other branches' asks into its own push diff. Removing the legacy path alone would have left the defect fully intact **while looking like a fix**.

## The real invariant

**A `paths:` filter cannot be the gate.** It cannot distinguish *"I asked for auto-merge"* from *"I merged somebody else's ask"* — the two produce an identical changed-file set. And the repo's own merge protocol tells branches to sync to `main`, so the condition fires most readily on the branches doing the right thing.

This is the **third** narrowing of that filter (`**` → `*.txt` on 2026-08-22, then this). The first two recurred, because narrowing a filter that cannot express the question is not a fix.

## What changed

1. **The request gate (job body, load-bearing).** The request file must be named for **this** branch and be **added-or-modified relative to `main`** — present-at-head plus a blob-sha comparison. A file inherited unchanged by a merge fails the second clause, which is exactly the mis-fire case. Two `getContent` calls, deliberately, rather than reading the push event's file list — the event's list is the thing that is wrong.
2. **The relay no longer calls `markPullRequestReadyForReview` at all.** A draft is this repo's "prepared, not approved" marker for Tier-2/Tier-3, and branch protection cannot defend it because it gates on **checks** and the checks are green. A PR the relay *creates* is born ready (that is the request being fulfilled); a draft anyone else opened is refused and left untouched.
3. `paths:` narrowed to the per-request glob only; legacy path removed.
4. A failed `getContent` **throws** rather than reading as "no request" — *we could not look* is not *it is not there*.

## The legacy file: DELETED, and why

Removed from the filter **and** deleted from the tree. Verified safe rather than assumed: **zero of the 14 open `claude/**` branches modify it** (`git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch> -- .github/pr-automerge-request` is empty for every one), and it was last modified 2026-08-21.

Leaving it inert-but-present was the alternative, and it is the worse one: its name still reads like a request, so a future session could write to it, believe it had asked, and be met with silence — a request that looks made and was not. Deleting it also removes the thing a future edit would re-add the path *for*.

## Negative control — both halves, and the controls are proven instruments

`tests/test_automerge_request_gate.py` runs the **shipped script**, extracted from the workflow YAML and evaluated under node against a mocked API. It does **not** re-implement the gate: a re-implementation is a second copy of the policy, free to drift from the one that actually decides, and this defect recurred twice precisely because the thing that decided was not the thing being reasoned about.

| | against **pre-fix** workflow | against **this** PR |
|---|---|---|
| negative: branch merged `main`, no own request | ❌ FAIL (`pulls.create`, `markReady`, `enableAutoMerge`) | ✅ pass — does nothing, doesn't even look for a PR |
| negative: slug-named file inherited unchanged from `main` | ❌ FAIL | ✅ pass |
| negative: draft PR + genuine request | ❌ FAIL (un-drafts it) | ✅ pass — refuses |
| negative: `getContent` 500 | ❌ FAIL (reads as absence, arms) | ✅ pass — throws |
| **positive: genuine request opens + arms** | ✅ pass | ✅ pass |
| **positive: modified request on an open non-draft PR arms** | ✅ pass | ✅ pass |

The negatives failing against the old workflow is what makes them instruments rather than tests that pass regardless; the positives passing against **both** is what shows the trigger was not simply broken. `5 failed, 2 passed` → `7 passed`.

## The mechanism that holds it (not a comment)

Per the operator's 2026-09-02 direction — *"I want actual guards and mechanisms in the repo/vm themselves"* — `scripts/ci/check_automerge_trigger.py`, registered **ungated** in `run_guards.py`.

Ungated is the point: a diff-scoped guard only fires when someone edits the relay, and **nobody was editing the relay when it armed three PRs**. The regression vector is a path landing on `main`. Same reasoning as `diagnostic-provenance-guard`'s ungated `--all` step, and survivable for the same reason — it is two file reads and the tree passes today.

It pins five things (filter exactly the per-request glob · legacy file absent · the slug is derived from the branch · the head/`main` comparison exists · `markPullRequestReadyForReview` unreachable in executable code), with a `--self-test` planting all six defects. **Two of my own plants initially failed and the self-test caught them** — one hit a comment instead of the YAML list entry, and the C4 check was matching incidental substrings. Both are fixed; the C5 check strips comments first, deliberately, so that the script's explanation of why it no longer un-drafts is not what fails CI.

## ⚠️ NOT FIXED BY THIS PR — two PRs are armed right now and I cannot disarm them

This change stops **new** mis-arming. It cannot retract auto-merge already enabled.

| PR | own request file? | its own body says |
|---|---|---|
| **#10788** `claude/decision-push-back` | none | *"Draft. Not for merge — it carries an operator decision."* |
| **#10764** `claude/claude-md-reference-split` | none | *"Left as a DRAFT. The manager owns the merge."* |

Both read `draft: false`. #10788's arming is confirmed from the run's own log, not inferred — run `33634977260` → `##[notice]auto-merge enabled on #10788 — merges when CI is green`. #10788 carries an **unanswered operator decision** about minting an account-wide `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`.

`update_pull_request` and `disable_pr_auto_merge` are **403** from this session. Filed as `BL-20260902-TWO-OPEN-PRS-ARE-ARMED-TO-MERGE-WHILE-THEIR-OWN-BODIES-SAY-DO-NOT-MERGE` (severity **critical**), whose resolution criteria require reading the state back from the API after acting — the arming was invisible to both authors, so a claim that it is undone is not the same as observing it.

## Verification

- `scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main`: **PASS 72 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 0**.
- `tests/test_automerge_request_gate.py`: **7 passed**; `5 failed, 2 passed` with the fix reverted.
- `check_automerge_trigger.py --self-test`: 6/6 planted defects caught, clean tree passes.
- `layer-guard` initially exited **127** — `lint-imports` was absent from the container. Installed and run: **6 contracts kept, 0 broken**. Environmental, verified rather than assumed.
- `artifact-validity-guard` caught a real defect of mine: I cited MI-62's sibling row id, which is filed only on the unmerged `claude/mi62/stop-unrequested-automerge` and resolves to nothing on `main`. Now named descriptively instead.

## Scope

Tier 1 — one workflow, one new CI guard, tests, docs, two backlog rows. Nothing touches `src/`, `config/`, an order path, risk caps, or a VM.

**This PR carries no `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt` of its own, deliberately** — given what it is fixing, it must not arm itself. Left as a **draft**; the manager merges.
